ei.title: A dog's welfare and assistance dog training
ei.subject: 수능특강Light

fullPassage: A dog's welfare includes psychological as well as biological or physical matters. It is wrong to turn your dog into a permanently chained watchdog, since being permanently tethered and isolated are both contrary to a dog's psychological welfare. Not all morally questionable arrangements, though, involve clearly visible cruelty or neglect, and here a major vulnerability of the model of raising assistance dogs surfaces. Recently, the treatment of assistance dogs has been questioned. Some researchers point out that sometimes pups are raised in foster homes with a lot of family interaction and then moved to individual kennels for months in their final training stages. What does this dramatic change do to the youngsters? One of them also notes that assistance dogs may have a series of human handlers during their lives. Since the pups are selected for their sociability, they bond with their handlers. How emotionally painful, then, is such a series of moves from one human or family to another? These potential welfare concerns do not involve psychological abuse. While we would likely describe months of isolation in kennels in final training as a straightforward welfare violation, we might also wonder how many moves from one home to another also count. * tether (밧줄이나 사술로) 매다 ** kennel 개집, 개 사육장

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

A dog's welfare includes psychological as well as biological or physical matters.

(A) Recently, the treatment of assistance dogs has been questioned. Some researchers point out that sometimes pups are raised in foster homes with a lot of family interaction and then moved to individual kennels for months in their final training stages.

(B) It is wrong to turn your dog into a permanently chained watchdog, since being permanently tethered and isolated are both contrary to a dog's psychological welfare.

(C) Not all morally questionable arrangements, though, involve clearly visible cruelty or neglect, and here a major vulnerability of the model of raising assistance dogs surfaces.

det.korean: 도입문에서 개의 복지가 심리적 측면까지 포함한다고 제시한 뒤, 구체적 사례로 이어지는 순서를 찾는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (B)-(C)-(A) ←정답

도입: 개의 복지는 심리적 측면을 포함한다.
→ (B): 영구적으로 묶어두는 것은 심리적 복지에 반한다는 구체적 예시 제시. 'permanently chained watchdog'이 도입문의 'psychological welfare'를 직접 설명.
→ (C): 'Not all ... though'로 전환하며 눈에 보이는 학대만이 아님을 지적. 'a major vulnerability of the model of raising assistance dogs surfaces'로 보조견 화제 도입.
→ (A): 'Recently'로 시작하며 (C)에서 언급한 보조견 모델의 문제를 구체적으로 전개.

❌ ① (A)-(B)-(C): (A)의 'Recently'가 도입 직후에 오면 보조견 화제가 갑작스러움.
❌ ② (A)-(C)-(B): (B)의 기본 예시가 (C)의 전환 뒤에 오면 논리적 역행.
❌ ④ (C)-(A)-(B): (B)의 기본 예시가 마지막에 오면 글의 흐름이 역전됨.
det.tip: 'Not all ... though'는 앞 내용을 인정한 뒤 전환하는 표현입니다.

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Some researchers point out that sometimes pups are raised in foster homes with a lot of family interaction and then moved to individual kennels for months in their final training stages.

(A) Since the pups are selected for their sociability, they bond with their handlers. How emotionally painful, then, is such a series of moves from one human or family to another?

(B) These potential welfare concerns do not involve psychological abuse. While we would likely describe months of isolation in kennels in final training as a straightforward welfare violation, we might also wonder how many moves from one home to another also count.

(C) What does this dramatic change do to the youngsters? One of them also notes that assistance dogs may have a series of human handlers during their lives.

det.korean: 위탁가정에서 개별 사육장으로의 변화 이후 논의가 어떻게 전개되는지 파악한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② (C)-(A)-(B) ←정답

도입: 강아지들이 위탁가정에서 자라다가 최종 훈련 단계에서 개별 사육장으로 옮겨진다.
→ (C): 'this dramatic change'가 도입문의 환경 변화를 직접 받음. 'One of them also notes'로 또 다른 연구자의 지적(핸들러 교체) 추가.
→ (A): 'Since the pups are selected for their sociability'로 (C)에서 제기한 핸들러 교체 문제의 원인 설명. 'a series of moves'가 (C)의 'a series of human handlers'와 연결.
→ (B): 'These potential welfare concerns'가 (C)+(A)의 우려를 총괄 정리. 'months of isolation in kennels'와 'moves from one home to another'를 비교하며 마무리.

❌ ① (A)-(C)-(B): (A)의 'Since'가 도입문 직후에 오면 핸들러 교체 맥락이 없어 비약.
❌ ③ (B)-(A)-(C): (B)의 총괄 정리가 먼저 오면 아직 논의되지 않은 내용을 요약하는 셈.
❌ ④ (C)-(B)-(A): (B)의 마무리가 (A)의 감정적 고통 언급 전에 오면 조기 결론.
det.tip: 'this dramatic change'의 지시 대상을 찾으면 첫 단락이 결정됩니다.

questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"Yet the emotional impact of repeated separations on these highly social animals deserves closer examination."

det.korean: 삽입 문장이 '반복적 분리의 감정적 영향'을 언급하므로, 핸들러 교체와 감정적 고통이 이미 논의된 뒤에 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① — 도입문 직후로, 아직 보조견이나 분리 이야기가 나오지 않은 시점.

❌ ② — 영구적 구속 사례와 보조견 모델 전환 사이로, 'repeated separations'의 맥락이 없음.

❌ ③ — 보조견 문제가 제기되기 시작하는 지점이지만 아직 핸들러 교체나 감정적 고통이 언급되지 않음.

✅ ④ ←정답 — 핸들러 교체로 인한 감정적 고통('How emotionally painful')이 제기된 직후이므로, 'repeated separations on these highly social animals'가 자연스럽게 요약·확장됨. 바로 뒤에 'These potential welfare concerns'가 이 삽입문까지 포함하여 총괄 정리.
det.tip: 'repeated separations'가 가리키는 내용이 앞에 이미 나왔는지 확인하세요.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: moving → moved: 수동태 병렬 구조 위반
det.analysis:
✅ ① being — 'since being permanently tethered and isolated are both contrary to ...' 동명사구가 주어 역할. 'being tethered'와 'isolated'가 병렬로 are에 호응.

✅ ④ their — 'they bond with their handlers'에서 복수 주어 they의 소유격으로 적절.
det.tip: 'are raised ... and then _____ to'에서 병렬 구조를 확인하세요.

questions.passage: A dog's welfare includes psychological as well as biological or physical matters. It is wrong to turn your dog into a permanently chained watchdog, since being permanently tethered and isolated are both contrary to a dog's psychological welfare. Not all morally questionable arrangements, though, involve clearly visible cruelty or neglect, and here a major vulnerability of the model of raising assistance dogs surfaces. Recently, the treatment of assistance dogs has been questioned. Some researchers point out that sometimes pups are raised in foster homes with a lot of family interaction and then moved to individual kennels for months in their final training stages. What does this dramatic change do to the youngsters? One of them also notes that assistance dogs may have a series of human handlers during their lives. Since the pups are selected for their sociability, they bond with their handlers. How emotionally painful, then, is such a series of moves from one human or family to another? These potential welfare concerns do not involve psychological abuse. While we would likely describe ______________________________ as a straightforward welfare violation, we might also wonder how many moves from one home to another also count.
